findings.finding: Insights: 2^20 players, 20 rounds, same‑score pairings → each player’s final score is a unique 20‑bit binary (wins per round). Any ordering of these binary strings can appear by suitable pairings, independent of speed order. Thus N = (2^20)! (all permutations). Compute v₂(N)=∑⌊2^20/2^i⌋, v₅(N)=∑⌊2^20/5^i⌋. k = min(v₂,v₅). Return k mod 10⁵.

Insights: Scores are binary 20‑bit win vectors; same‑score pairing forces a perfect binary tree. Final ranking depends only on which speed‑orderings are compatible with a binary tournament. Count permutations realizable → N = (2^{20})! / (product of leaf‑group sizes). Compute v₂(N), v₅(N); k = min(v₂,v₅). Beware double‑counting ties and that each internal node must have faster winner. Use recursion: for a node with m runners, any split into two equal groups of m/2 is allowed, then faster group must be winner side. This yields N = ∏_{i=0}^{19} (2^{20-i})!^{2^{i}}. Then v₅(N)=∑_{i=0}^{19}2^{i}·v₅((2^{20-i})!). Compute similarly for v₂. Finally k = min(v₂,v₅) mod 100000.

Insights: 20‑round Swiss with points 2^{19}…1 gives each player a 20‑bit win vector. Pairings only split equal‑score groups; winners are faster in each pair. Final scores are binary numbers; ties occur when players share the same win vector. N = number of distinct total orderings (including permutations within ties) achievable over all pairing choices. Compute exponent of 10 in N. Pitfall: decide if permutations of tied players count; likely they do not (orderings treat ties as equal).

Insights: Winners each round must be matchable to slower losers → sequence of “W/L” (slow→fast) never has more Ws than Ls. Thus after round i, possible score‑bit patterns correspond to Dyck paths of length 2·2^{20‑i}. Number of final rankings = product of Catalan numbers C_{2^{19}}·C_{2^{18}}·…·C_{1}. Compute N’s 10‑adic valuation k = Σ v₁₀(C_{2^{m}}) (m=0..19). Use v₁₀ = min(v₂,v₅). v₂(C_n)=# carries when adding n+n in binary; v₅(C_n)=# carries when adding n+n in base 5. Sum over n=2^{m}. Then k mod 10⁵. Pitfall: ensure Catalan count valid for each round; pairings independent across rounds.

Insights: After i rounds each i‑bit binary score appears 2^{20‑i} times. Final scores are all 2^{20} distinct binary strings. A round i splits each equal‑score group into winners/losers of size half; winners must be a “Dyck” subset (prefix #wins≥#losses). Thus each round’s feasible winner sets = Catalan C_{2^{20‑i‑1}}. Multiply Catalan numbers for i=1..20 to get N. Compute k = ν_{10}(N) = min(ν_2(N),ν_5(N)). Find ν_2,ν_5 via Legendre sums on factorials in Catalan formula. Return k mod 10^5.

Insights: Final scores are binary strings of length 20; each round splits each equal‑score group into exactly half winners (must be faster than paired losers). Feasible winner sets S of size n/2 in a group of n must satisfy Hall: for any top‑k fastest, winners ≥⌈k/2⌉. This yields a Catalan‑type count of possible binary trees → N = product of central binomial coefficients. Compute k = ν₁₀(N) and output k mod 10⁵.

Insights: Final scores are distinct 20‑bit strings; ranking = lexicographic order of these strings. The tournament builds a perfect binary tree of depth 20. At each node (size 2^m) we must choose a left half (winners) of size 2^{m‑1} that contains the fastest leaf of that node and omits its slowest leaf. Recursively apply to both halves. N = product over all internal nodes of the number of admissible left‑half choices. For a node of size 2^m, the count = C(2^m‑2, 2^{m‑1}‑1) (choose remaining 2^{m‑1}‑1 winners after fixing fastest in left and slowest forced to right). Thus  

\[
N=\prod_{m=1}^{20}\Bigl(\binom{2^{m}-2}{2^{m-1}-1}\Bigr)^{2^{20-m}} .
\]

Compute v₂(N) and v₅(N) via Legendre’s formula on each binomial, then k=min(v₂,v₅). Finally output k mod 10⁵. Pitfalls: ensure exponent 2^{20‑m} for each level (number of nodes of that size); handle large binomial valuations efficiently.

Insights: After 20 rounds each runner gets a unique 20‑bit score. The tournament’s choices equal choosing, at every internal node of a perfect binary tree (size 2ⁿ), a “Dyck” split of its leaves – exactly C_{size/2} ways.  

Thus  
\(N=\prod_{r=0}^{19}C_{2^{r}}^{\,2^{19-r}}\).

Compute prime valuations:  
\(v_2(N)=\sum_{r=1}^{19}2^{19-r}=2^{19}-1=524287\).  
\(v_5(N)=\sum_{r=0}^{19}2^{19-r}\,v_5(C_{2^{r}})=121818\) (non‑zero only for r≥3).  

\(k=\min(v_2,v_5)=121818\).  
Answer: \(k\bmod10^{5}=21818\).  

Pitfalls: assume all scores distinct (true), treat each node independently, use Catalan count (Dyck condition) not just “top half”.

Insights: Final scores are distinct binary strings of length 20. Each round splits a group of size 2^m into winners/losers; feasible winner sets are exactly Dyck subsets → Catalan C_{2^{m‑1}} ways.  
Thus  
\(N=\prod_{m=2}^{20}C_{2^{m-1}}^{\,2^{20-m}}\).  

Prime‑valuations: for n=2^i, \(v_2(C_n)=1\); \(v_5(C_n)=\) carries when adding n+n in base 5 minus \(v_5(n+1)\). Compute for i=1…19 (n=2^i):  

v5 values: 0,0,1,1,0,2,1,0,1,1,3,3,4,0,2,3,5,4,6.  

Sum weighted by 2^{19‑i}: \(v_5(N)=121 818\); \(v_2(N)=2^{19}‑1=524 287\).  

k = min(v2,v5)=121 818.  
Answer = k mod 100 000 = **21818**.  

Pitfalls: ensure carries count final overflow; size‑2 groups give C₁=1 (no factor).

Insights: Final rankings equal product of Catalan splits at each node. N = ∏_{m=1}^{20} Catalan_{2^{m-1}}^{2^{20-m}} where Catalan_n = C(2n,n)/(n+1). Compute v₂(N), v₅(N) via Legendre on binomials and subtract vₚ(n+1). k = min(v₂,v₅). Pitfall: ignore extra factorials—product already counts all orderings. Use exponent formulas for each factor, sum weighted by 2^{20-m}.

Insights: Scores are binary strings of wins; all 2²⁰ distinct, so final ranking is a permutation. A round splits a group into winners/losers; the winner set must be a “ballot” (Dyck) subset → Catalan Cₙ choices for n=2^{j}. Recurrence: f₁=1, f_{k}=C_{2^{k-1}}·f_{k-1}². Hence  
N=f_{20}=∏_{j=0}^{19}C_{2^{j}}^{2^{19-j}}.  

Valuations: v₂(C_{2^{j}})=1 (j≥1),0 (j=0); v₅(C_{2^{j}})=v₅(binomial(2·2^{j},2^{j}))−v₅(2^{j}+1). Compute via Kummer (carries in base 5).  

Result: v₂(N)=2^{19}−1=524 287; v₅(N)=121 818.  
k=min(v₂,v₅)=121 818 → k mod 10⁵ = **21818**.  

Pitfalls: assume ties (none); ensure ballot condition for splits; use Catalan count, not all subsets.

Insights: Scores are binary strings of length 20. In each round a group of 2^m players splits into equal halves; the winners’ set must satisfy the “Dyck” (ballot) condition → C_{2^{m‑1}} choices. Splits at different nodes are independent.  

Result:  
\(N=\prod_{j=0}^{19}C_{2^{j}}^{\,2^{19-j}}\) with \(C_n=\frac1{n+1}\binom{2n}{n}\).  

Compute valuations:  
\(v_2(N)=\sum_{j}2^{19-j}v_2(C_{2^{j}})=524287\)  
\(v_5(N)=\sum_{j}2^{19-j}v_5(C_{2^{j}})=121818\).  

\(k=\min(v_2,v_5)=121818\).  

Answer: \(k\bmod10^5=21818\).  

Pitfalls: assume all scores distinct (true); ensure Dyck condition is both necessary & sufficient for a feasible winner set.

Insights: Final scores are distinct 20‑bit numbers; ranking = leaf order of a perfect binary tree. Each round splits a set of size 2ⁿ into equal halves with “ballot” (Dyck) condition → Catalan C_{2^{n‑1}} ways.  
Thus  
\(N=\prod_{t=1}^{20}C_{2^{t-1}}^{\,2^{20-t}}\).  

\(k=v_{10}(N)=v_{5}(N)=\sum_{r=1}^{19}2^{19-r}\,v_{5}(C_{2^{r}})\).  
Compute \(v_{5}(C_{2^{r}})=v_{5}((2·2^{r})!)-2v_{5}((2^{r})!)-v_{5}(2^{r}+1)\).  
Summing gives \(k=121 818\).  
Answer: \(k\bmod10^{5}=21 818\).  

Pitfalls: assume scores distinct (true by binary weights); use Catalan, not binomial; ensure v₂(N)>v₅(N).
